finding.claim: Malicious SCP server can write files outside the chosen download directory: a leading 'E' record decrements directoryCounter to -1 without a matching 'D', so the ==0 exit never fires and each E moves the write target up one ancestor, after which C records create server-chosen files there.
finding.source: Server-controlled SCP protocol stream read in InternalDownload (ScpClient.cs:895); entry via Download(string, DirectoryInfo) at ScpClient.cs:520. Precondition: victim downloads a directory from an attacker-controlled server or via MITM when host key is not pinned (see F3).
finding.sink: fileInfo.Open(FileMode.Create) at ScpClient.cs:966 on new FileInfo(Path.Combine(currentDirectoryFullName, fileName)) at ScpClient.cs:963

trace.note: server's first record read as 'E' (no preceding D)
currentDirectoryFullName moved to parent (Debug.Assert at 910 compiled out in Release)
Path.Combine(ancestor, name) used as write target
file created and filled with server bytes
counter != 0 so loop continues; further E records climb higher

finding.guards_checked: EnsureValidLocalName (ScpClient.cs:840-854) rejects '.', '..', empty and invalid filename chars, but only validates the name component, not the cursor position. The break at :903 and :979 uses exact ==0 with no clamp on directoryCounter. No check that currentDirectoryFullName stays under the original destination. Matches expertise case 20 (zip-slip) invariant applied to the directory cursor.

finding.claim: Default DoubleQuote remote-path transform does not escape backslash, so a path containing \" closes the shell string early and allows arbitrary remote command execution (e.g. path '\"; id #/x' yields exec 'scp -t -d "\\"; id #"'). $() and backticks also expand inside the double quotes.
finding.source: Caller-supplied remote path (e.g. a user-provided filename) passed to ScpClient.Upload/Download. Precondition: the obsolete ScpClient constructors (default transform, ScpClient.cs:159-163 and :270-298) or explicit RemotePathTransformation.DoubleQuote, with an untrusted path value.
finding.sink: channel.SendExecRequest with interpolated transformed path, ScpClient.cs:367 and :410 (also :459, :498, :538, :578); executed by the remote shell.

trace.note: CreateAbsoluteOrRelativeFilePath splits on '/' only; no sanitization (PosixPath.cs:45-69)
only '"' is escaped (line 63); '\\' and '$' and backtick are passed through
remote sh parses "\\"; id #" as closed string, then ';' starts command 'id', '#' comments the rest

finding.guards_checked: Only the [Obsolete] warning on the constructors. PosixPath performs no metacharacter handling. The opt-in RemotePathShellQuoteTransformation (RemotePathShellQuoteTransformation.cs) was checked and is correct, so this affects only the DoubleQuote default. Did not test against a live server.

finding.claim: Host key trust defaults to accepting any key with a valid signature when no HostKeyReceived handler is attached, so a MITM can impersonate the server and receive subsequent credentials.
finding.source: Network attacker (MITM) or malicious server. Precondition: application does not subscribe to Session.HostKeyReceived (Session.cs:383).
finding.sink: Session establishment and subsequent authentication (credentials sent to attacker-controlled peer).

trace.note: handlers = HostKeyReceived; null when no subscriber
return true when no handler attached

finding.guards_checked: Signature verification (KeyExchange.cs:493) proves the server holds the presented key only, not that the key is expected. Session.cs:383 documentation does not state the accept-by-default behaviour. May be intentional API design; flagged as unsafe default.

finding.claim: SCP upload writes server-directed protocol record 'C0644 <size> <name>\n' with unvalidated name; an embedded newline in the remote destination file name or local file name injects extra SCP protocol records into the remote scp sink. Low confidence: impact not tested.
finding.source: Caller-supplied remote path or local file name containing a newline. Reaches via posixPath.File (ScpClient.cs:374, :420) or file.Name (:801).
finding.sink: SendData of formatted protocol record to remote 'scp -t' (ScpClient.cs:649).

trace.note: string.Format("C0644 {0} {1}\n", fileSize, serverFileName) with no newline check

finding.guards_checked: None on the name component. Impact depends on remote scp sink parsing of injected records, which was not verified.

finding.claim: UNVERIFIED hypothesis: On Windows, Path.GetInvalidFileNameChars() excludes space and dot, so a name like '.. ' (trailing space) passes EnsureValidLocalName; Win32 path normalization may trim it to '..' and allow parent-directory traversal in SCP download writes.
finding.source: Server-controlled filename in SCP C/D record on a Windows client.
finding.sink: Path.Combine / FileInfo open in ScpClient.cs:932 and :963.

trace.note: EnsureValidLocalName compares only for exact '.' and '..' and invalid chars

finding.guards_checked: Exact-match '.'/'..' check and invalid-char check at ScpClient.cs:847-850. Not testable on this macOS host; no Windows run performed.
